findings: 12 cases: 3 containers x 2 destinations x 8/10-bit AV1. Six native frames per case pass independent component and rational PTS readback.

Disk writes preserve an existing prefix and restore stream end; three-byte writes and initial Interrupted are qualified. IVF uses one four-byte patch, progressive MP4 one eight-byte patch, WebM none. Forward-only routes have no patches.
IVF has zero of six explicit packet durations in independent inspection; WebM and MP4 preserve six of six. This is not permission to silently discard a required duration.
With an authored 40 ms decode/presentation origin, IVF/WebM/fragmented MP4 preserve PTS. Progressive MP4 refuses at finish after 1748 appended bytes in the fixture.
Shared driver validates track epochs/clocks before native effects; partial header errors preserve I/O causes and confirmed append counts; cancellation/timeout between writes is terminal.
Invalid final patch preflight changes neither tail nor previous bytes. In-memory apply_finish is deprecated in favor of MuxFinish::apply_to; external writers use validate.

limits: The driver is private; no public checked timing/layout admission is implemented by this trial.
Synchronous short-write sink and real disk files; no HTTP or async backpressure throughput claim.
Pending byte lengths are observed buffers, not allocations or whole-operation bounds.
Encoded output is staged after native encoder completion; input owners and native/mux workspaces remain outside admission.
The zero pixel-change count excludes unresolved planar conversion and rendering contracts.
Resource lines describe validation processes, not native codec/mux memory or comparative performance.
